newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRENCHMAN GINOLA HINTS AGAIN OF A RETURN HOME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCHMAN GINOLA HINTS AGAIN OF A RETURN HOME.

text.p: Newcastle winger David Ginola hinted again on Tuesday he was ready to return to France -- but not before the end of the season.

Ginola, who has started in only two of Newcastle's five matches under new coach Kenny Dalglish, said he would be keen to play for either his former team Paris St Germain or their arch-rival Marseille.

"Nothing is done yet. But if an opportunity shows up. I'd love to play for my local team, but perhaps that might not happen," Ginola said in a interview with the French sports daily L'Equipe on Tuesday.
"I never said explicitly that I wanted to leave to come back to Paris or to join Marseille. I won't talk about leaving before the end of the season", the former French international winger said.
Ginola was in Paris at the weekend where he recorded a television show for the pay-per-view channel Canal Plus but he did not meet with the PSG vice-president Michel Denisot.
In fact sources in France say the 30-year old striker would be more likely to join Marseille, which is where he is orignally from.
"I am in debt to Marseille's fans," he said.
"I would like to come back to my country (the South) like the prodigal son. I love my country and I feel very close to it."
Ginola also expressed his fears about top players like himself leaving the French league for the higher salaries offered in England, Italy and Spain.
"The people in charge in the French football must do something to keep the players. Our soccer is going downhill," he said.
Ginola should get a chance to show his French fans what they are missing when Newcastle face Monaco in their UEFA Cup quaterfinal next month.
Ginola joined Newcastle for 4.5 million pounds ($ 7.05 million) in the summer of 1995 from Paris St Germain and has become a great favourite of the Geordie fans.
If he did move Newcastle would probably expect around 5.0 million for him.
